hints: Focus on the two observations together, you need a reaction that makes both a colourless gas and a new white solid.
Think about what gas a metal gives with dilute acid, and what gas a carbonate gives with dilute acid or water.
Now check solubility, which sulfate or chloride product would actually appear as a white precipitate in excess acid while the other products stay in solution?
walkthrough:
**List what must happen**

X is a solid that disappears or reacts in excess Y. You must form a colourless gas and also form a different white solid as a product.

Rule to use: metal + acid gives salt + $\text{H}_2$, carbonate + acid gives salt + $\text{CO}_2$ + $\text{H}_2\text{O}$

**Check the gas possibilities**

Metals Ca and Mg with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ would give colourless $\text{H}_2$ gas. Carbonates $\text{BaCO}_3$ and $\text{SrCO}_3$ with acid would give colourless $\text{CO}_2$ gas, but $\text{BaCO}_3$ with just $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ gives no reaction and no gas.

**Check the precipitate possibilities**

The key is Group 2 solubility. $\text{MgSO}_4$ is very soluble so no precipitate. $\text{SrCl}_2$ is soluble so no precipitate. $\text{CaSO}_4$ is sparingly soluble and forms a white precipitate.

$$\text{Ca(s) + H}_2\text{SO}_4\text{(aq)} \rightarrow \text{CaSO}_4\text{(s) + H}_2\text{(g)}$$

**Confirm precipitate is not X**

Here X is grey Ca metal, while the white solid is new $\text{CaSO}_4$. This fits all three conditions: colourless $\text{H}_2$, white precipitate, and precipitate is not the starting solid.

options.A: $\text{BaCO}_3$ is insoluble in water and does not react with $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ to give a gas. No colourless gas and no new precipitate would be seen, so this fails both observations.
options.B: Ca reacts vigorously with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to give colourless $\text{H}_2$ gas and white sparingly soluble $\text{CaSO}_4$ as a precipitate. The precipitate is a new product, not the original Ca metal, so all conditions are met.
options.C: Mg with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ does give colourless $\text{H}_2$ gas, but the product $\text{MgSO}_4$ is soluble. No white precipitate would be seen, only a colourless solution, so students who forget the solubility trend choose this trap.
options.D: $\text{SrCO}_3$ with dilute HCl does give colourless $\text{CO}_2$ gas, but the product $\text{SrCl}_2$ is soluble. No white precipitate forms in excess acid, so this fails the second observation.
